subject: after "unite" with destrand=TRUE I got multiple lines for the same genomic position

messages.author: 34f8ff1f2f6869a1
messages.subject: after "unite" with destrand=TRUE I got multiple lines for the same genomic position
parts:
Hello,

I am running methylKit_9.0.2 on R version 3.0.2 (2013-09-25) (using RStudio Version 0.98.501). I had the following observation with the "unite" function.

Let's start from the beginning: get file list - import files - filter - unite:

> library(methylKit)
> file.list=list("control.txt" ,"treatment.txt")
> samples = read(file.list, sample.id=list("control", "treatment"), assembly="hg19", treatment=c(0,1))

> samples.filtered=filterByCoverage(samples,lo.count=10,lo.perc=NULL, hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)
> samples.filtered.united=unite(samples.filtered,destrand=TRUE)


now let's look for a specific position in the genome, chr10:135000000 (I am subsetting for an interval around that position):

> subset(getData(samples.filtered.united), chr=chr10, start > 134999900 & start < 135000200)

468336 chr10 134999993 134999993      +       64    58     6

Manual calculation for destranding based on the filtered object reveals that:
the first line in the unite object (line #354440 - see above) is correct.
the other three lines are:

line #354441: sample 1 correctly united and sample 2 shows the values for genomic position 135000001 only
line #354442: sample 1 only genomic position 135000001 and sample 2 correctly united
line #354443: sample 1 and 2, both only position 135000001

any ideas why this happens?

I was digging a bit deeper and found the following things which I am just briefly outlining here.

- running the unite function with "destrand=FALSE" is working fine - so I guess this is really a problem of the destranding.

- I found the same problem at another genomic position: chr2:165000000

- all other positions in the genome give only one line after unite. 

- So what is special about those two problematic positions? As you see, both (chr10:135000000 and chr2: 165000000) end on 6 zeros - so I hypothesised this could be some number crunching problem and checked if I have calls on other genomic positions ending with "000000". Indeed I found a few more, but they behaved all fine. Finally, I found the following characteristics that our two problematic friends have in common (and that are different from the other positions ending on "000000"): Both are on the + strand and the corresponding position (+1) on the minus strand is covered (i.e. destranding has something to do). For all the other positions ending with "000000" those positions are either on the - strand, or, if it they are on the + strand, the corresponding position on the - strand is not covered. I hope that helps a bit.

I would be thankful if somebody could look at that and let me know any thoughts. Thanks a lot.

Thorsten

Hi Thorsten,
if you made sure that none of your files have duplicates, you can try the development version and see if the problem persists, but you have to make sure there are no duplicate positions in any of the files.

Best,
Altuna
